recipes.title: Lemon-Herb Chicken Thighs
recipes.description: Crispy-skinned chicken roasted over lemony potatoes with garlic and thyme. One pan, almost no fuss, and the kind of dinner that makes the kitchen smell like a Sunday.
recipes.imageAlt: Golden roasted chicken thighs and drumsticks on a white plate.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Pat the chicken thighs thoroughly dry, then season both sides with salt, pepper, smoked paprika, and the lemon zest.
Toss the potatoes with olive oil, garlic, dried thyme, and another pinch of salt. Spread them in a single layer in a large roasting pan or ovenproof skillet.
Nestle the chicken, skin-side up, among the potatoes. Add the lemon slices to the pan. Do not crowd the chicken — the skin needs room to crisp.
Roast for 30–35 minutes, until the skin is deep golden and a thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 175°F (79°C).
If the skin needs more colour, move the pan to the top rack and broil for 2–3 minutes. Watch it closely.
Rest for 5 minutes, scatter with parsley if using, and spoon the pan juices over the potatoes before serving.
recipes.notes: No fresh thyme? Use 1 teaspoon of dried thyme in the potatoes and tuck a few rosemary sprigs around the chicken if you have them. The pan juices are the best part — serve this with crusty bread to mop them up.

recipes.title: Smoky Black Bean Tacos
recipes.description: Charred tortillas, creamy chipotle beans, and all the crunchy things. A 25-minute dinner that is happy to be made from the pantry.
recipes.imageAlt: Two crispy black bean tacos with lettuce, sour cream and rice on a white plate.
steps: Warm the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Add half the red onion and cook for 3 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, chipotle, and cumin and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the black beans and 1/4 cup water. Season with salt, bring to a simmer, and cook for 6–8 minutes, mashing about a third of the beans with a fork until the mixture is creamy but still chunky.
While the beans cook, char the tortillas directly over a gas burner for 20–30 seconds per side, or warm them in a dry skillet. Wrap them in a clean towel to stay soft.
Taste the beans and adjust: more chipotle for heat, a squeeze of lime for brightness, salt if it tastes flat.
Pile the beans into warm tortillas. Top with avocado, the remaining red onion, cilantro, feta if using, and a good squeeze of lime.
recipes.notes: The beans keep for four days in the fridge and freeze well. For a vegan version, skip the feta and add pickled jalapeños or a spoonful of salsa macha.

recipes.title: Sunday Beef Ragù
recipes.description: A slow-simmered, deeply savoury ragù with red wine, tomatoes, and a whisper of bay. Make it on a grey afternoon and let the house do the work.
recipes.imageAlt: Tagliatelle tossed with rich beef ragù and fresh herbs in a white bowl.
steps: Pat the beef dry and season generously with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a heavy Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in batches, giving each piece room, until deeply browned on all sides. Set aside.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onion, carrot, and celery with a pinch of salt. Cook for 8–10 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until the vegetables are soft and sweet.
Add the garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the paste darkens to brick red.
Pour in the wine and simmer for 3 minutes, scraping the bottom of the pot. Return the beef and any juices to the pot.
Add the crushed tomatoes, stock, and bay leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook on low for 2 1/2–3 hours, stirring every 30 minutes, until the beef pulls apart with a fork.
Uncover and simmer for 20–30 minutes to thicken the sauce. Taste and adjust the salt. Fish out the bay leaves.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water until just shy of al dente. Toss with a few ladles of ragù in the pot, adding pasta water as needed. Serve with parmesan and basil.
recipes.notes: The ragù is better the next day and freezes beautifully for up to three months. If you do not cook with wine, replace it with the same volume of beef stock plus a tablespoon of balsamic vinegar.

recipes.title: Buttermilk Blueberry Pancakes
recipes.description: Tall, fluffy pancakes with bursting blueberries and crisp edges. The batter comes together in one bowl, which is exactly what weekend mornings require.
recipes.imageAlt: A small stack of blueberry pancakes with maple syrup and fresh blueberries on a white plate.

ingredients.note: melted, plus more for the pan

steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In a second bowl, whisk the buttermilk, eggs, melted butter, and vanilla until smooth. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold just until no dry streaks remain. A few lumps are good.
Let the batter rest for 5 minutes while the griddle heats over medium. Fold in the blueberries last, so they do not dye the whole batter blue.
Lightly butter a nonstick griddle or skillet. Scoop about 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles appear across the surface and the edges look set, about 2–3 minutes.
Flip and cook for 1–2 minutes more, until golden. Keep finished pancakes on a plate under a clean towel while you cook the rest.
Serve hot with maple syrup and extra blueberries.
recipes.notes: No buttermilk? Stir 1 tablespoon lemon juice into 1 1/2 cups milk and let it sit for 10 minutes. Freeze leftover pancakes in a stack with parchment between them; reheat in the toaster.

recipes.title: Ginger-Scallion Noodles
recipes.description: A fast, punchy bowl of noodles tossed in ginger-scallion oil, soy, and chili crisp. Faster than delivery and twice as good.
recipes.imageAlt: Ginger scallion noodles topped with cucumber and mushrooms in a dark blue bowl.

ingredients.note: thinly sliced, whites and greens separated

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cook the noodles according to the package, then drain, reserving 1/2 cup of the cooking water.
While the water heats, combine the scallion whites, ginger, and garlic in a heatproof bowl.
Warm the neutral oil in a small saucepan over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Pour it carefully over the aromatics — it will sizzle. Stir and let it steep for 2 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, rice vinegar, chili crisp, and sugar if using. Whisk to combine.
Toss the hot noodles with the sauce, adding a splash of noodle water until glossy and well coated. Scatter with scallion greens and sesame seeds. Taste and add more soy or chili crisp as needed.
recipes.notes: This is a pantry recipe, so make it yours: add a fried egg, a handful of spinach wilted into the hot noodles, or leftover roast chicken. The ginger-scallion oil can be made a day ahead and kept in the fridge.

recipes.title: Roasted Tomato Soup & Grilled Cheese
recipes.description: Jammy roasted tomatoes blitzed into a velvety soup, served with a properly crisp grilled cheese. The lunch that fixes most things.
recipes.imageAlt: A bowl of roasted tomato soup with a toasted grilled cheese sandwich on a yellow plate.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Toss the tomatoes, onion, and garlic with olive oil, salt, and pepper on a large sheet pan. Arrange the tomatoes cut-side up.
Roast for 25–30 minutes, until the tomatoes are collapsed and the onion edges are charred in spots. Let cool for a few minutes.
Transfer everything on the pan, including the juices, to a blender. Add the vegetable stock and blend until completely smooth. (Work in batches if your blender is small.)
Return the soup to a pot and warm gently. Stir in the cream if using. Taste and adjust the salt and pepper. Keep warm while you make the sandwiches.

Butter one side of each slice of bread. Build the sandwiches with cheddar between the unbuttered sides. Cook in a skillet over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes per side, pressing lightly, until the bread is deep golden and the cheese has fully melted.
Ladle the soup into bowls, shower with basil if using, and serve with the grilled cheese cut on the diagonal.
recipes.notes: The soup freezes well before the cream is added. For a plant-based version, use olive oil instead of butter on the bread and a good vegan cheddar — the soup itself is already dairy-free without the cream.

recipes.title: Chocolate Olive Oil Cake
recipes.description: A one-bowl chocolate cake with a tender, almost brownie-like crumb. Olive oil keeps it moist for days and makes it taste grown-up.
recipes.imageAlt: A thick slice of dark chocolate layer cake with chocolate drizzle and cream on a white plate.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9-inch round cake pan, line the bottom with parchment, and grease the parchment.

In a large bowl, whisk the flour, cocoa, baking soda, and salt. Add the sugar, olive oil, eggs, milk, and vanilla. Whisk until smooth, then slowly whisk in the hot espresso. The batter will be thin — that is correct.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake for 35–40 minutes, until the centre springs back and a skewer comes out with just a few moist crumbs.
Cool in the pan for 15 minutes, then turn out onto a rack to cool completely.
Dust with powdered sugar just before serving. Slice with a hot, dry knife for clean edges.
recipes.notes: The cake is even better on day two, wrapped tightly at room temperature. It also freezes well for up to two months. Serve with slightly sweetened whipped cream or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

recipes.title: Charred Broccoli Grain Bowl
recipes.description: Deeply roasted broccoli, warm quinoa, crispy chickpeas, and a lemony tahini drizzle. A desk lunch worth looking forward to.
recipes.imageAlt: Charred broccoli florets over rice in a shallow white bowl.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Cook the quinoa with 2 cups water and a pinch of salt: bring to a boil, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it steam, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Toss the broccoli and chickpeas with olive oil, smoked paprika, and salt on a large sheet pan. Spread everything into a single layer.
Roast for 18–22 minutes, shaking the pan once, until the broccoli edges are charred and the chickpeas are crisp.
Whisk the tahini, yogurt, garlic, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. Add water a spoonful at a time until the dressing pours easily.
Pile the quinoa into bowls. Top with the roasted broccoli and chickpeas, and spoon the tahini dressing over the top. Scatter with pumpkin seeds if using.
Serve warm, or portion into containers for lunch. Keep the dressing separate until serving.
recipes.notes: For a vegan dressing, swap the yogurt for extra tahini and a teaspoon of maple syrup. The components keep separately in the fridge for four days — assemble bowls as you go.
